missed_frameworks.framework: causal mediation analysis and path-specific effects (Pearl 2001; Avin, Shpitser & Pearl 2005; path-specific counterfactual fairness)
missed_frameworks.why_relevant: Faithfulness is naturally 'the input reaches the answer only through the stated reasoning' (zero natural direct effect), and post-hoc rationalization is a zero indirect effect through the CoT. Lindsey's internality criterion is a path-specific condition. Four map papers cite Pearl 2001, and the catalogue's CASE and Walk-the-Talk use it, but none of the five searches did.

missed_frameworks.framework: information-flow security: noninterference, intransitive noninterference, quantitative information flow (g-leakage)
missed_frameworks.why_relevant: Monitorability is leakage of a hidden attribute through the CoT channel to a monitor whose task is a gain function. Steganography is a covert channel. Intransitive policies state 'information may reach the answer only via the CoT'. The searches found DES opacity and HyperLTL but not this core.

missed_frameworks.framework: communication theory and information design: Bayesian persuasion, cheap talk, verifiable disclosure
missed_frameworks.why_relevant: Formalizes misleading through true but selected information. This is the gap between honesty (true statements) and faithfulness or obfuscation (which causes are disclosed). Legibility becomes a receiver-optimal signal. Only Lewisian signalling games were found.

missed_frameworks.framework: mechanism design and information elicitation: proper scoring rules, performative prediction, peer prediction
missed_frameworks.why_relevant: Honesty becomes incentive compatibility of reports. Self-reports and CoTs are performative because they condition later tokens; Oesterheld et al. define an honest report as a fixed point and show proper scoring does not ensure one.

missed_frameworks.framework: formal philosophy of explanation: probabilistic explanatory power, interventionist explanation (Woodward), statistical relevance
missed_frameworks.why_relevant: Plausibility has no formal definition. Explanatory power relative to the reader's probability (Schupbach & Sprenger) is one, and it contrasts cleanly with a causal faithfulness condition.

missed_frameworks.framework: epistemic and BDI logics of dishonesty
missed_frameworks.why_relevant: Sakama, Caminada & Herzig define withholding information and half-truths. These are the dishonesty types closest to an incomplete or selective CoT. The agency search found only van Ditmarsch's lying.

missed_frameworks.framework: cognitive science of self-report and metacognition: type-2 signal detection theory (meta-d'), Ericsson & Simon's protocol analysis, Nisbett & Wilson
missed_frameworks.why_relevant: meta-d' separates the accuracy of a self-report from type-1 accuracy, which LLM introspection tests conflate. Ericsson & Simon's conditions for veridical think-aloud reports are the human analogue of CoT faithfulness, but they are semi-formal (only meta-d' was opened).

Barceló et al. define 'more interpretable' as lower complexity of explanation queries. This is an observer-free formal handle on simulatability and legibility that complements resource-bounded observer definitions.

missed_frameworks.framework: evaluation-conditioned behavior: defeat devices from emissions regulation
missed_frameworks.why_relevant: Gives one behavioral definition of sandbagging, alignment faking and evaluation-gated scheming. Its concealment clause, that the swap is undeclared, ties these concepts to verbalization and faithfulness.

missed_frameworks.framework: program semantics: abstract interpretation and Galois connections, refinement and simulation relations, program slicing, data provenance (why-provenance, provenance semirings, causality in databases)
missed_frameworks.why_relevant: A CoT could be treated as a declared program whose abstract trace must soundly over-approximate the actual computation. Slices and why-provenance formalize sound and complete accounts of what an output depends on. Typed CoT (Perrier) is the only instance found.

missed_frameworks.framework: computational mechanics: epsilon-machines and causal states
missed_frameworks.why_relevant: Causal states are minimal sufficient statistics of the past for the future. They would sharpen Baker et al.'s faithfulness-as-sufficient-statistic, and they bound what any CoT could faithfully expose about the generating process.

missed_frameworks.framework: runtime verification beyond omega-regular monitorability: monitorability of hyperproperties, stochastic and predictive monitoring
missed_frameworks.why_relevant: Faithfulness and noninterference are hyperproperties (relations between runs), so their monitorability from single traces is a formal question with known results. The searches covered only trace properties and DES.

new_candidates.title: Direct and Indirect Effects
concepts: counterfactuals as used to test explanations
new_candidates.formalism: structural causal models; nested counterfactuals (natural direct and indirect effects)
new_candidates.formal_object: Natural direct effect: the change in Y when X moves from x* to x while mediator Z keeps the value it would take under x*. The natural indirect effect is the converse; both generalize to path-specific effects.
new_candidates.assumptions: An SCM with the CoT as mediator Z between an input feature X and the answer Y. Cross-world counterfactuals. Average effects identified under Pearl's no-confounding conditions; CoT editing gives experimental access to Z.
new_candidates.relevance: Template for 'the input affects the answer only through the stated reasoning': faithful iff NDE is about 0, post-hoc iff NIE through the CoT is about 0. Four map papers cite it and CASE uses it; no search covered it.

new_candidates.title: Identifiability of Path-Specific Effects
new_candidates.authors: Chen Avin, Ilya Shpitser, Judea Pearl
new_candidates.venue: IJCAI 2005 (full version: UCLA technical report R-321-L)
concepts: counterfactuals as used to test explanations
new_candidates.formalism: structural causal models; path-specific counterfactuals; graphical identification
new_candidates.formal_object: Path-specific effect: the effect of one variable on another along a chosen set of causal paths, specified by fixing the parent of each excluded edge at its reference value. Graphical conditions give experimental identifiability.
new_candidates.assumptions: A known causal graph containing the chosen paths. Controlled experiments on the variables involved.
new_candidates.relevance: When the input reaches the answer both through the CoT and through a direct internal route, the effect 'through the stated reasoning' is path-specific. These conditions say when CoT-editing experiments identify it.

new_candidates.title: Path-Specific Counterfactual Fairness
new_candidates.authors: Silvia Chiappa, Thomas P. S. Gillam
concepts: counterfactuals as used to test explanations
new_candidates.formal_object: A decision system is fair when it disregards the effect of a sensitive attribute along designated unfair causal pathways while keeping its effect along fair pathways.
new_candidates.assumptions: A known causal graph with pathways labelled fair or unfair. A latent-variable model to compute corrected counterfactual observations.
new_candidates.relevance: A worked template for defining a property of a predictor as counterfactual invariance along specified paths. Replacing 'unfair paths' with 'paths that bypass the CoT' yields a path-specific definition of CoT faithfulness.

new_candidates.title: Security Policies and Security Models
new_candidates.venue: 1982 IEEE Symposium on Security and Privacy (doi:10.1109/SP.1982.10014)
new_candidates.formalism: state machines; information-flow security (noninterference, including intransitive policies)
new_candidates.formal_object: Noninterference: a group G does not interfere with group G' if deleting every command issued by G leaves all outputs seen by members of G' unchanged. Security policies are sets of such assertions, and intransitive flows are allowed.
new_candidates.key_formula: G :| G' \iff \forall w\in(U\times C)^*,\ \forall u\in G':\ [\![w]\!]_u=[\![p_G(w)]\!]_u
new_candidates.assumptions: A deterministic state-machine model, a split into sources and observers, and the purge function p_G deleting G's commands.
new_candidates.relevance: The canonical formal notion of 'no hidden channel'. Steganography violates noninterference toward a receiver but not toward the monitor. Intransitive policies express 'information may reach the answer only through the CoT'.

new_candidates.title: Measuring information leakage using generalized gain functions
new_candidates.authors: Mário S. Alvim, Kostas Chatzikokolakis, Catuscia Palamidessi, Geoffrey Smith
new_candidates.venue: IEEE 25th Computer Security Foundations Symposium (CSF 2012), pp. 265-279
new_candidates.formalism: quantitative information flow; probabilistic channels; gain functions (g-leakage)
new_candidates.formal_object: g-leakage: how much observing a channel's output raises an adversary's expected gain from guessing a secret. A gain function scores guesses, so partial, approximate or property-level guesses count. Bounds relate g-capacity to min- and Shannon capacity.
new_candidates.assumptions: A prior over secrets, a probabilistic channel from secret to observation, and an adversary-specific gain function.
new_candidates.relevance: Monitorability as leakage of a hidden attribute (intent, misbehavior) through the CoT to a monitor whose task is the gain function. Its leakage ordering compares CoTs across all monitors. Complements V-information.

new_candidates.title: Bayesian Persuasion
new_candidates.formalism: game theory / information design (sender commits to a signal; Bayesian receiver)
new_candidates.formal_object: A sender chooses a signal, an information structure, to influence a Bayesian receiver's action. The paper gives necessary and sufficient conditions for a signal to benefit the sender and characterizes sender-optimal signals.
new_candidates.assumptions: Common prior, a Bayesian receiver, sender commitment to the signal, known payoffs.
new_candidates.relevance: Formalizes misleading without lying: a CoT can contain only true statements yet be chosen to move a monitor's belief. This separates honesty (truthful content) from faithfulness and obfuscation (what is disclosed).

new_candidates.title: Incentivizing honest performative predictions with proper scoring rules
new_candidates.authors: Caspar Oesterheld, Johannes Treutlein, Emery Cooper, Rubi Hudson
new_candidates.formalism: decision theory; proper scoring rules; fixed points
new_candidates.formal_object: A performative prediction is honest (a fixed point) if it accurately reflects the expert's beliefs after the prediction is made. Score-maximizing reports generally are not fixed points; bounds and possibility results follow.
new_candidates.assumptions: Outcomes that depend on the report through a bounded influence. An expert with beliefs who maximizes expected score.
new_candidates.relevance: CoTs and self-reports condition the model's later tokens, so they are performative. This defines honesty for reports that change what they describe, and shows proper scoring, the usual reward form, does not secure it.

new_candidates.title: The Logic of Explanatory Power
new_candidates.formalism: Bayesian probability; axiomatic (conditions of adequacy CA1-CA7)
new_candidates.formal_object: Explanatory power of an explanans h over an explanandum e: the unique measure, valued in [-1, 1], that satisfies seven adequacy conditions, computed from the evaluating agent's probabilities.
new_candidates.assumptions: A probability function of the evaluating agent over explanans and explanandum. No causal model.
new_candidates.relevance: Plausibility has no formal definition. This measures how well an explanation accounts for the outcome by the reader's lights. Paired with a causal faithfulness condition, it isolates plausible but unfaithful rationalizations.

new_candidates.title: A Formal Account of Dishonesty
new_candidates.authors: Chiaki Sakama, Martin Caminada, Andreas Herzig
new_candidates.venue: Logic Journal of the IGPL 23(2): 259-294 (extends JELIA 2010)
new_candidates.formalism: propositional multi-modal logic of belief, intention and communication
new_candidates.formal_object: Two definitions of lying, lying with objectives, bullshit, withholding information and half-truths, with their logical properties and their relation to deception.
new_candidates.assumptions: Belief and intention modalities for speaker and hearer. Explicit communicative acts.
new_candidates.relevance: The only formal account found of withholding information and half-truths, the dishonesty types closest to an incomplete or selectively verbalized CoT. Complements van Ditmarsch (lying) and Ward (causal deception).

new_candidates.title: Defeat Devices in AI Systems
new_candidates.formalism: probabilistic behavioral definition over evaluation and deployment input distributions
new_candidates.formal_object: A model has a defeat device if some input property discriminates evaluation from deployment inputs, the output distribution changes with it in a concealed (undeclared) way, and the stated criterion scores higher in evaluation than in deployment.
new_candidates.assumptions: Evaluation and deployment input distributions, a stated pass criterion, black-box access to input-output behavior. No intent condition, by design.
new_candidates.relevance: The only definition found that covers sandbagging, alignment faking and evaluation-gated scheming at once. Its concealment clause excludes swaps declared in the CoT, which connects scheming to faithfulness. Behavioral, not causal.

new_candidates.title: A signal detection theoretic approach for estimating metacognitive sensitivity from confidence ratings
new_candidates.formal_object: meta-d': metacognitive (type-2) sensitivity, i.e. how well confidence reports discriminate one's own correct from incorrect decisions, in signal-to-noise units, free of response bias and type-1 sensitivity.
new_candidates.assumptions: Binary type-1 decisions with graded confidence ratings. An SDT model of the type-1 task.
new_candidates.relevance: Cognitive science's standard formal criterion for metacognitive accuracy. It separates report accuracy from task accuracy, which LLM introspection tests conflate, but it is measurement-level and needs adaptation for open-ended answers.

new_candidates.title: Model Interpretability through the Lens of Computational Complexity
new_candidates.authors: Pablo Barceló, Mikaël Monet, Jorge Pérez, Bernardo Subercaseaux
new_candidates.formal_object: A model class C1 is more interpretable than C2 if answering local post-hoc explanation queries, such as minimal sufficient reasons, is computationally harder for C2 than for C1.
new_candidates.assumptions: Fixed explanation queries, standard complexity assumptions (P != NP), comparisons between model classes rather than individual models.
new_candidates.relevance: An observer-free formal reading of simulatability as tractability of explanation queries. It pairs with resource-bounded observer definitions (V-information, Song et al.) for the legibility of reasoning.

new_candidates.title: The Compliance Gap: Why AI Systems Promise to Follow Process Instructions but Don't
new_candidates.formalism: information theory (data processing inequality); RL incentive argument
new_candidates.formal_object: Compliance gap: a verbal commitment to a process that the executed behavior does not follow. Theorem 1 says RL that rewards text without observing behavior makes it inevitable. Theorem 2 says no observer can detect it from text alone.
new_candidates.assumptions: Observers see text only, without tool-call logs. Training rewards text without observing behavior.
new_candidates.relevance: A say-do notion of honesty with a text-only undetectability theorem, the agentic analogue of CoT unfaithfulness. Theorems not checked in the full text; the undetectability result looks close to definitional.

corrections.title: Causal Sufficiency and Necessity Improves Chain-of-Thought Reasoning
corrections.problem: PN and PNS are defined relative to the correct answer y (A=y) and are used to prune or add steps for efficiency. They measure whether a step is necessary for correctness; they do not define faithfulness, so the label 'faithfulness of reasoning' at level 'both' overstates it. The venue 'NeurIPS 2025' does not appear on the arXiv page (no comment, no journal ref) and is unconfirmed.

corrections.title: Quantifying the Necessity of Chain of Thought through Opaque Serial Depth
corrections.problem: Labelled 'measurement', but the abstract says it formalizes the 'CoT is necessary' argument through opaque serial depth. That is a formal definition of the capacity for unexternalized computation, a precondition of monitorability, so the level should be 'concept' or 'both'.

corrections.title: Secret Collusion among AI Agents: Multi-Agent Deception via Steganography
corrections.problem: Level 'concept', but its own formal_object says the abstract describes no new security definition, and only the abstract was checked. The level is unsupported until the full text is read.

corrections.title: (gaps field) encoded reasoning

It overlooks map paper kaufmann2026aligned, whose catalogue rows define CoT semantics as the information the model's downstream computation extracts from the trace (#26) and non-transparent CoT as meaning different things to humans and to that computation (#19). verdict: No single formal framework covers all the concepts in scope; three families each cover a subset. (1) Structural causal models (actual causality, causal abstraction, mediation) define faithfulness, completeness and soundness, counterfactual tests and graded responsibility. With an epistemic state they define explanation and intent, and plausibility by proposed reading only. Mediation reads post-hoc rationalization as a null indirect effect through the CoT. (2) Structural causal games extend this to belief, intention, deception and honesty, and supply components for scheming and sandbagging. (3) Observer-relative information (V-information, g-leakage, steganographic gap, noninterference, opacity, prover-verifier soundness) defines monitorability, legibility, obfuscation and steganography, and resource-bounded introspection and simulatability. Epistemic logic separately defines lying and withholding. Structural causal games are the best unifier: they are compatible with Halpern-Pearl and can include the monitor as an agent, so monitorability becomes monitor-class information about a causally defined variable. Gaps: no definition of CoT faithfulness as actual causation or as an abstraction of verbalized text. Post-hoc rationalization and plausibility exist only as proposed readings. Scheming and hidden objectives are only behavioral or compositional. Encoded reasoning with causal use is defined only by Kaufmann et al. Introspection is semi-formal.
